chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, both together from Ibn Mahboub from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying regarding a.s. ) saying regarding a man who killed a woman deliberately, so he ( a.s. ) said: 'If her family so desire, they can kill him, and pay half the wergild to his family; and if they so desire, they can take half the wergild of five thousand Dirhams'.

And he ( a.s. ) said regarding a woman who killed her husband deliberately, so he ( a.s. ) said: 'If his family so desire, they can kill her for his killing, and no one reaps more than the crime upon himself'.
ai.seo_question: What are the rules of Qisas and Diyah when a man kills a woman versus a woman kills a man in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi clarifies the asymmetry in Qisas (retaliation) and Diyah (blood money) between genders, noting that while a man's life is valued at double that of a woman's in compensation, the principle of 'no more than the crime' ensures the female perpetrator faces execution without a financial penalty differential. It highlights the juristic consensus that the right to execute rests with the victim's family, who may choose between capital punishment or accepting the reduced wergild of 5,000 Dirhams. This ruling underscores the Shia interpretation of equity in retribution, balancing the quantitative difference in wergild with the qualitative equality in the right to life.
